parts.title: Secure Container

parts.title: Care Package
parts.summary: Execute an Intcode arcade cabinet program producing (x, y, tileId) output triples until halt and return the count of destructible block tiles (tileId = 2) on the screen.
parts.algorithmSummary: Read-only reuse of complete 2019/shared/intcode/ via O(1) cursor-draining ArcadeIoChannel and run-first pause/resume loop paired with polymorphic ArcadePolicy (BLOCK_COUNT_POLICY for Part 1, pre-built FREE_PLAY_SCORE_POLICY patching memory[0]=2 with reactive joystick tracking sign(ballX - paddleX) for zero-churn Part 2) in 2019/day13/shared/ (13.42 ms across 989 tiles -> 363 blocks): O(<= 120)-clone memory-bounded dual-mode trace replay, 9-primitive batched 5-band Atari Breakout rainbow CRT SVG visualizer with single-pass VM execution, differentially verified against an independent flat-loop Intcode reference oracle.
parts.complexity: O(V + E) time, O(W * H) solve space
learnings: Recording compact ArcadeEvent deltas and cloning the screen Map only on the <= 120 sampled trace indices avoids allocating thousands of Map snapshots during Part 2 Breakout playback.
Adding formatFrameAnswer(frame) onto ArcadePolicy lets the visualizer derive the final answer directly from the guaranteed terminal trace frame without running the Intcode VM twice.

parts.title: Care Package
parts.summary: Patch memory address 0 to 2 for free play, steer the Breakout paddle underneath the ball via joystick inputs (-1, 0, +1) until all blocks are cleared, and return the final segment-display score.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2019/day13/shared/ and read-only 2019/shared/intcode/ binding FREE_PLAY_SCORE_POLICY into ArcadeSolver and ArcadeCabinetVisualizer (362.93 ms across full Breakout match -> 17,159): zero edits to shared/, part1/, or shared/intcode/, immutable program.withPatches([{ address: 0n, value: 2n }]), reactive sign(ballX - paddleX) autopilot, Segment Score Display banner and 18-point ball trajectory trail, differentially verified across a 235-int reactive Breakout ROM (testing +1/0/-1 tilts and score progression 0 -> 45 -> 12345), relative-base segment displays, and error boundaries against an independent flat-loop Intcode oracle.
parts.complexity: O(V + E) time, O(M + W * H) space
learnings: Pre-building FREE_PLAY_SCORE_POLICY, ArcadeScoreBanner, and O(<= 120)-clone play-phase replay in day13/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 4 lines and beat the full Breakout cabinet in 363 ms with zero shared edits.

Because FREE_PLAY_SCORE_POLICY unconditionally patches mem[0] = 2 (MUL), synthetic Part 2 Intcode test tapes must start with a patch-safe 4-cell preamble like 1,0,0,<scratch> rather than immediate-mode 104 or 99.

parts.title: Space Stoichiometry
parts.summary: Compute the exact minimum BigInt quantity of raw ORE needed to synthesize 1 unit of FUEL through a DAG of whole-batch chemical reactions with surplus pooling.
parts.algorithmSummary: Single-pass reverse-topological BigInt demand propagation reusing read-only shared/core DirectedGraph (topologicalOrder + relevantSubgraph) and ceilDiv, with polymorphic StoichiometryPolicy (ORE_FOR_ONE_FUEL_POLICY for Part 1, pre-built exponential-bracketing binary search MAX_FUEL_FOR_TRILLION_ORE_POLICY for zero-churn Part 2) in 2019/day14/shared/ (1.89 ms across 60 reactions -> 899,155 ORE): zero-derived-state ChemicalDemand/FuelSearchStep/DagLayout, left-to-right layered DemandWaterfallSvg & log-scale FuelSearchGaugeSvg visualizer, differentially verified across all 5 official Part 1 examples, all 3 official Part 2 examples, and 20 seeded random DAGs against independent surplus-inventory FIFO and linear-scan oracles.
parts.complexity: O(V + E) Part 1 / O((V + E) log B) Part 2 time, O(V + E) space
learnings: Validating closed reactant references and full-graph acyclicity via DirectedGraph.topologicalOrder() BEFORE pruning unused reactions with relevantSubgraph('FUEL', 'ORE') prevents undefined chemicals or ORE-disconnected cycles from being silently dropped.
Requiring fuelAmount > 0n in evaluateStoichiometry while starting findMaxFuelForOre at low = 0n eliminates unreachable zero-demand branches while handling budgets < ore(1n) cleanly.

parts.title: Space Stoichiometry
parts.summary: Compute the exact maximum integer quantity of FUEL that can be synthesized from a cargo hold of 1,000,000,000,000 ORE using pooled reaction surplus.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2019/day14/shared/ binding MAX_FUEL_FOR_TRILLION_ORE_POLICY into StoichiometrySolver and StoichiometryVisualizer (2.94 ms -> 2,390,226 FUEL): zero edits to shared/ or part1/, exponential bracketing + exact BigInt binary search over monotonic reverse-topological oreRequiredForFuel, log2-scale [low, high] bracket & ORE budget gauge in FuelSearchGaugeSvg, differentially verified via tightness invariant oracleOre(ans) <= 10^12 < oracleOre(ans + 1) across all 3 official examples, extreme 10^24 BigInt scale, and 25 seeded PRNG DAGs against an independent coalesced FIFO surplus-inventory simulator.
parts.complexity: O((V + E) log F) time, O(V + E) space
learnings: Pre-building MAX_FUEL_FOR_TRILLION_ORE_POLICY and FuelSearchGaugeSvg in day14/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 4 lines and computed max FUEL from 1 trillion ORE in 2.94 ms with zero shared edits.

Checking the two-sided tightness invariant oracleOre(ans) <= budget < oracleOre(ans + 1n) with an independent coalesced FIFO surplus-inventory simulator proves global optimality without duplicating binary search.

parts.title: Oxygen System
parts.summary: Navigate a remote Intcode repair droid through an unmapped ship compartment via movement commands (1=N, 2=S, 3=W, 4=E) and return the fewest commands from the origin to the oxygen system.
parts.algorithmSummary: Single-VM iterative DFS backtracking explorer + O(V) cursor-queue BFS over read-only 2019/shared/intcode/ with O(1) DroidIoChannel and polymorphic OxygenPolicy (SHORTEST_PATH_POLICY for Part 1, pre-built OXYGEN_FILL_MINUTES_POLICY for zero-churn Part 2) in 2019/day15/shared/ (47.95 ms -> 354 steps): zero VM cloning, full cyclic-maze exploration, non-leaf oxygen backtracking safety (accepting status 1 or 2 on return), pure-TS <= 8-primitive SVG layout (vizLayout.ts), light-mode ShipCompartmentVisualizer blueprint playback, differentially verified on the compiled 87-int official 5x4 maze ROM (P1 = 2, P2 = 3), cyclic shortcut mazes, and 8 protocol-error boundaries.
parts.complexity: O(V * C_step + V) time, O(V) space
learnings: Exploring the full connected compartment with a single IntcodeMachine via physical reverse-command DFS backtracking avoids VM cloning and guarantees true shortest paths on cyclic mazes while pre-mapping the entire compartment for Part 2.
Backtracking onto a non-leaf oxygen cell can legitimately return status 1 or 2, so backtrack validation must reject only status 0 while forward duplicate-oxygen checks remain branch-clean.

parts.title: Oxygen System
parts.summary: Once the oxygen system is repaired, determine how many minutes it takes for oxygen to diffuse orthogonally across every reachable open tile in the ship compartment.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2019/day15/shared/ and read-only 2019/shared/intcode/ binding OXYGEN_FILL_MINUTES_POLICY into OxygenSystemSolver and ShipCompartmentVisualizer (48.71 ms -> 370 minutes): zero edits to shared/, part1/, or shared/intcode/, single-VM DFS backtracking explores the full connected component then O(V) head-index queue BFS computes exact eccentricity from the oxygen cell, oxygen wavefront SVG playback, differentially verified on the compiled 97-int official 6x5 Part 2 example ROM (4 minutes), cyclic ring/asymmetric/pocket fixtures, and 24 seeded PRNG bordered mazes against an independent ASCII Set<string> diffusion oracle.
parts.complexity: O(V * I + V) time, O(V) space
learnings: Pre-building OXYGEN_FILL_MINUTES_POLICY, full-compartment DFS exploration, and oxygen-wavefront SVG playback in day15/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 4 lines with zero shared-module edits.

Compiling the exact official 6x5 Part 2 example (8 open cells, 4 minutes) into a 97-int Intcode ROM keeps Part 2's live manifest example faithful to the Part 2 prompt rather than reusing Part 1's 5x4 corridor.
